display_label: US casual-dining restaurant group 401(k) plan (~$1.6B, FL)
anonymization_rule: Sponsor name NEVER appears on demo surfaces. Data is public (DOL Form 5500 FOIA files); anonymization is a project display rule, not a legal requirement.

source.publisher: DOL EBSA Form 5500 FOIA bulk files (2024 Latest)

plan_characteristics.codes_decoded: 2E profit sharing; 2F ERISA 404(c) plan; 2G total participant-directed; 2J 401(k) arrangement; 2K employer match; 2T default investment account (QDIA); 3F additional characteristic code as filed
plan_characteristics.note: 404(c) + fully participant-directed = designated-investment-alternative framework squarely applies

benefit_payments_2e.reason: not typed: Schedule H line 2e is not yet in the plan record
benefit_payments_2e.source: Schedule H line 2e (benefit payments and payments to provide benefits)

participant_contributions_2a1b.reason: not typed: Schedule H line 2a(1)(B) is not yet in the plan record

qdia_indicator.reason: the Form 5500 does not code a QDIA election. The plan document or the 404a-5 participant disclosure does, and neither is in the record
qdia_indicator.source: plan document or 404a-5 participant fee disclosure

filed_outflow_proxy.unit: percent of beginning-of-year net assets, per plan year
filed_outflow_proxy.formula: (total expenses minus total administrative expenses) / net assets at the beginning of the plan year * 100

net_assets_boy.meaning: net assets at the beginning of the plan year, Schedule H

source.publisher: DOL EBSA Form 5500 FOIA bulk files (2024 Latest)

filed_outflow_proxy.what: a proxy for the plan's filed outflow rate while Schedule H line 2e (benefit payments) is not in the record. Total expenses less administrative expenses is an upper bound on benefit payments, because the remainder also holds the non-administrative expense lines the schedule reports besides benefits. The inputs are the financials block of this record, whose source is the source block above
filed_outflow_proxy.used_as: the base demand of the liquidity scenario layer: this rate applied to the plan's position in a product, compared with the wrapper's annual repurchase capacity. The turnover sliders are the stress around it, never the base

dictionary_cells.3.7 participant liquidity demand: high-turnover hourly workforce: 197,946 active participants vs only 43,129 accounts with balances - most actives hold no balance yet; separated tail 12,176 (28.2% of accounts); small average balances and frequent cash-outs dominate flows
dictionary_cells.3.7 filed outflows (schedule_h.benefit_p: when typed, the liquidity match prints the filed outflow rate benefit_payments_2e / net_assets_boy as a Schedule H line 2e figure beside the filed outflow proxy. Until then the match says the line is not yet in the plan record and the proxy stands in for it
dictionary_cells.3.7 filed inflows (schedule_h.participan: when typed, printed as an inflow rate that offsets outflows at the plan level, never at the position level
dictionary_cells.3.5 QDIA (schedule_h.qdia_indicator): when typed, the structural reasons name the QDIA and state that a product reaching participants through it sits inside a TDF or managed-account sleeve, not as a standalone DIA
dictionary_cells.3.7 filed outflow proxy (schedule_h.file: the base demand of the scenario layer: 10.75% of beginning net assets per year, (tot_expenses - tot_admin_expenses) / net_assets_boy, recomputed and checked by the validator on every run
